objectives: Use sick-child visits to identify missed immunization opportunities.
Distinguish true contraindications from mild illness that still allows vaccination.
Plan catch-up immunization with clear caregiver communication.
takeaways: Mild cough/coryza without severe illness is usually not a contraindication to vaccination.
Checking the child health card during every visit prevents missed opportunities.
Catch-up schedules should be practical, documented, and explained in plain language.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A child presents with mild cough, but the immunization card shows missed vaccines.

rows.label: Missed doses
rows.value: Measles and booster not yet given

coach.title: Denis came for cough, but card tells a bigger story
coach.body: The clinical task includes both acute care and prevention.

coach.title: Should immunization be deferred?
coach.body: Use true contraindications, not fear-based assumptions.

question.prompt: What is the best decision now?

options.text: Proceed with catch-up vaccination if eligible while managing mild cough
Defer all vaccines until child has zero cough symptoms for a month
Ignore immunization card during sick-child visits
Start antibiotics first, then decide about vaccines next year

question.right: Correct. Mild illness without danger signs is not usually a reason to miss scheduled catch-up vaccination.
question.wrong: Automatic deferral creates missed opportunities and prolongs vulnerability to vaccine-preventable disease.

sections.title: Visit plan
sections.detail: Treat mild cough supportively and give due immunizations per schedule

sections.title: Counseling points
sections.text: Discuss expected post-vaccine reactions and next appointment date.

coach.title: What should you tell the caregiver?

options.text: Explain why vaccines are still safe today, document next doses, and give return advice
Tell caregiver vaccination is optional since child is older now
Give vaccines but avoid discussing possible minor side effects
Focus only on cough and omit immunization documentation

question.right: Correct. Confidence and clarity improve adherence to catch-up schedules and reduce future missed opportunities.
question.wrong: Incomplete counseling and poor documentation lead to repeated gaps in immunization coverage.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You addressed mild acute illness and closed a missed immunization gap in the same visit.
sections.emphasis: Every child visit is also a prevention checkpoint.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: HC III sick-child care should routinely include card review and catch-up action when no contraindication exists. This prevents avoidable outbreaks and delayed protection.
